`await` on something that is not a promise gives back the same value one tick later. It usually means the `await` is in the wrong place: on an array of promises instead of `Promise.all()`, or on a function instead of its call.

The rule does not use types. It reports literals, arrays, template strings, functions, classes, JSX, another `await`, and the results of operators such as `+`, `!` and `typeof`. A variable, a call or an object literal may be a promise, so those are not reported.

`--fix` removes the `await` where that is safe.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```js
async function load(ids) {
  const users = await [fetchUser(ids[0]), fetchUser(ids[1])];
  const retries = await 3;
  const total = await (users.length + retries);
  return total;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
async function load(ids) {
  const users = await Promise.all([fetchUser(ids[0]), fetchUser(ids[1])]);
  const retries = 3;
  const settings = await (cached || fetchSettings());
  return users.length + retries + settings.extra;
}
```
